quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. If the vehicle needs to move, it could block your escape route. Speed up or drop back to get away from the other vehicle.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the most important thing you can do to be seen at an intersection. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to have a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance does not matter for safety.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Always the right side of the lane.
Always the center of the lane.
Always the left side of the lane.
It depends on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road conditions, weather, and traffic.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake on the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat (if you know which one that is).

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
Look over your shoulder and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see traffic around you.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet or vest helps other drivers see you. Use it during the day and night.

questions.question: Before you ride, your pre-ride check should include everything below except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a full pre-ride check each time.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Push the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you clear the hazard.

questions.question: When entering a curve, how should a group ride?
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you through turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should proceed with caution. Look both ways before crossing the intersection.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?
questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of your lane.
Do not worry about where you ride in the lane.
Always ride on the far right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. The driver is most likely to see you there in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow what they say.

questions.question: What is the best riding position?

options.text: You use your arms to hold yourself up.
You can reach the controls easily.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees do not touch the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can reach the controls easily.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. You should not have to stretch to reach them. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back as possible on the seat.

questions.explanation: A passenger should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as you can without getting in the operator's way. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When do most crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles. They happen just a few minutes after the rider starts out.
